results.content:
The New York Fed’s Survey of Consumer Expectations for July, released on Aug. 7, shows short-term inflation expectations edged down by 0.1 percentage point while medium and longer-term held steady. Perceptions about the current financial situation improved from a year ago, with a larger share of households reporting a better financial situation compared to those reporting a worse one. The perceived likelihood of losing a job in the next 12 months increased, as did the perceived probability of [...] Inflation. Median one-year inflation expectations fell by 0.1 percentage point to 3.6%. Medium-term expectations were unchanged at 3.3%, as were longer-term expectations at 3.0%.

results.content: Inflation expectations among consumers have also begun to soften. The New York Fed reported in early August that median inflation expectations at the one-year-ahead horizon decreased by 0.1 percentage point to 3.6 percent in July, suggesting that households are becoming more confident that price pressures will moderate going forward. results.content: This is also the first time that consumer sentiment has deteriorated in three months. Consumer expectations for inflation over the next 12-month period rose to 4.3% in August from 4.2% in July. The five-year, or long-term inflation expectations index remained unchanged at 3.3%.
